rows.title: Unclear subscription enrolment
rows.problem: Customers do not realise they are enrolling in a subscription, and are surprised by later charges and orders.
rows.why_it_matters: This is the only item on the list that costs money rather than support time. Recurring charges a customer does not remember authorising are the single biggest driver of chargebacks, and a high dispute rate puts the payment processor at risk. Unclear enrolment of this kind is also a specific enforcement target for the FTC's negative-option rules in the US.
rows.metric: Chargeback rate, and cancellations at the second charge

actions.text: Audit the checkout: is the subscription pre-selected, and are the amount and the frequency shown next to the buy button?
Post-purchase email in plain language: this is a subscription, the next charge is on <date>, cancel here.
Reminder email a few days before every charge.
Self-serve cancellation in the customer portal, without contacting an agent.
Refund without argument when a customer says they did not know. Cheaper than a chargeback.

rows.title: Delivery delays
rows.problem: Customers report long waits and excessive delays, generating a high volume of support contacts.
rows.why_it_matters: The largest single source of ticket volume. Contact volume here falls by telling the customer before they ask, not by shipping faster.
rows.metric: Where-is-my-order tickets as a share of orders, and real transit time per supplier

actions.text: Proactive email when tracking has not moved for X days. This is what removes the most volume.
Take the delay data to the supplier and agree on a concrete improvement.

rows.title: Missing items in multi-packs
rows.problem: A customer buys a pack of several units and receives one. A 5-pack of socks arrives as a single pair. Happening across different products.
rows.why_it_matters: Every case is a refund or a reshipment, so it costs margin on top of the support time.
rows.metric: Missing-item tickets per 1,000 orders, by product

actions.text: Pull the affected orders and list which products and pack sizes are involved — the supplier conversation needs this to be specific.
Work with logistics to establish why multi-packs ship short, and agree how it stops happening.

rows.title: Wrong size shipped
rows.problem: The customer orders one size and receives another — an M arriving as an XL, for example. Happening across different products.
rows.why_it_matters: In dropshipping the return shipping usually costs more than the item, so almost every case ends as a refund or a free reshipment.
rows.metric: Wrong-size tickets per 1,000 units, by product

actions.text: Check the size conversion table between the supplier's sizing and the sizing sold on the store.
Talk to the supplier about why it is happening and how it stops.

rows.title: Wrong colour shipped
rows.problem: Customers receive the product in a colour other than the one they ordered.
rows.why_it_matters: Same cost shape as the wrong-size cases, and it may share the same root cause in how variants map to supplier items.

actions.text: Talk to the supplier about why it is happening and how it stops.

rows.title: Address changes arriving too late
rows.problem: The customer asks to change the delivery address, but the order has already been processed or shipped to the previous one.
rows.why_it_matters: A parcel sent to the wrong address is usually a total loss, not a delay.
rows.metric: Address-change requests, and parcels returned as undeliverable

actions.text: Add address validation at checkout — an app that checks the address as the customer types it and warns when it looks wrong, so fewer changes are needed at all.
